# Power an assistant workflow: Slack for voice, webhook

**Pattern:** AI Agent · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers voice work end to end across Slack, Google Sheets and Microsoft Teams.

It moves through 15 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Receive Inbound Webhook
2. Collect Raw Text
3. Extract Structured Fields
4. Anthropic Chat Model
5. All Required Fields Found?
6. Upsert into Google Sheets
7. Queue for Manual Review
8. Merge Review Paths
9. Cap Batch Volume
10. Guard Non-Empty message
11. Sort Conversations Newest First
12. Stamp Processing Time
13. Summarize Run Stats
14. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
15. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing voice work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Receive Inbound Webhook → Collect Raw Text → Extract Structured Fields → Anthropic Chat Model → All Required Fields Found? → Upsert into Google Sheets → Queue for Manual Review → Merge Review Paths → Cap Batch Volume → Guard Non-Empty message → Sort Conversations Newest First → Stamp Processing Time → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Slack and Google Sheets aligned by hand for voice
- Pushing voice events into Slack and Google Sheets the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Voice work where "Collect Raw Text" is still a manual step before Slack
- Voice work that only reaches Slack when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Slack and Google Sheets in step for voice, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Slack or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 17 nodes in this voice build
- Branches rejoin before Slack, so a voice run reports once rather than 17 times
- Fans the same result out to Microsoft Teams in the same run, for voice
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 17 nodes for voice before wiring Slack

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Anthropic API key; Google OAuth2 / service account; Microsoft OAuth2; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The required-fields check runs *before* the write, not after — an incomplete extraction goes to manual review instead of landing a half-populated record in the system of record. Upsert (not plain create) means re-processing the same document twice updates the existing record instead of duplicating it.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Add a new field to the extraction schema and mark it required — watch more documents route to manual review.
2. Feed it a document deliberately missing a required field and trace exactly where it ends up.
3. Change the extraction target (e.g. invoice → contract fields) and adjust the upsert key to match.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Anthropic API key**
console.anthropic.com → Settings → API Keys.
_Gotcha:_ Requires purchased credit.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.
_Gotcha:_ Graph throttles with HTTP 429 — the retry setting on this node already handles it.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Microsoft Teams: restrict the app registration to the target team; tenant-wide permission is not needed to post.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole voice payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your voice process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
